slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only slot/copy in the image: a single 0x2000-byte block at SRAM offset 0 is transferred by the sole 0x0E000000 call site (FUN_08015154 from FUN_0801a6a8). No backup copy, mirroring, or generation counter exists; bytes 0x2000..0x7FFF are never written. Validity is hypothesised to be gated by the magic at offset 0.

checksums.name: none_found_candidate_u32_at_0x28_rejected
checksums.formula_detail: No stored checksum exists in the populated sample. The only candidate word (u32_le at 0x28 = 0x084A1097) was tested against sum8, sum16, sum32, xor8, CRC32, sum of u16_le words and sum of u32_le words over the full 0x2000 block and sub-ranges (0x10..0x2000, 0x20..0x2000, 0x2C..0x2000, 0x00..0x28, and full block excluding the candidate word); no computed value matches any stored byte/word in the block. The candidate value's top byte 0x08 places it in the GBA ROM window, i.e. it reads as a persisted ROM pointer, not a digest. Post-transfer integrity in code is read-back verification via FUN_0801ccbc, not a stored digest. verified_on_samples below records the CRC32 test as the representative falsification.

io_driver_functions.notes: Boot orchestrator (MMIO seed). Zeroes a large RAM work struct, calls FUN_08015154(0x0E000000, _DAT_0801a818, 0x2000), then initialises subsystems (FUN_08019774, FUN_08019dd8, FUN_0801a3ac, FUN_08013e38, FUN_08014028(0), FUN_08015af0(0), FUN_0800310c(0)). Read-at-boot direction is a strong hypothesis; payload direction unrecovered.

Transfer-descriptor setup: stores {addr_a, addr_b, len} into *_DAT_080151bc, calls FUN_0801520c, then strcmp-like FUN_08019f1c (args dropped by Ghidra); on mismatch strcpy FUN_08019ee8 into descriptor+0x10 and sets descriptor words [0xc]=[0xd]=1; sets halfword flag at descriptor+0xC.

Transfer via RAM-copied payload FUN_0801cb44(desc[0], desc[1], desc[2]), then verify pass FUN_0801ccbc(desc[1], desc[0], 0x94); on non-zero result stores status and strcpys an error label. Called via func_ spelling, so absent from callgraph.json callees.

Sibling flush path: byte copy FUN_0801cc1c(desc[1], desc[0], desc[2]) then the same FUN_0801ccbc verify + error handling. FUN_0801cc1c provably copies param1->param2, so with the boot descriptor values this is RAM->SRAM. NO static caller in callgraph.json; reachable only via unrecovered jumptable dispatch.
Byte-at-a-time copy: param1=src, param2=dst, param3=count (proven from body). Correct primitive for 8-bit SRAM bus.

SRAM wrapper: read-modify-write of a wait-state register (& mask | 3, consistent with WAITCNT 0x04000204), copies a halfword code block from ROM (address ^1) onto the stack, tail-calls FUN_0801cda4(p1, p2, p3, stack+1). Discards result.

Same RAM-copied-payload wrapper as FUN_0801cb44 but returns FUN_0801cda4's result; used as the post-transfer verify/read-back pass (third argument 0x94, meaning unknown). Role recorded as checksum in the sense of integrity verification; it computes no stored digest.
RAM-copied SRAM payload executed from the stack. Body is an UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE in Ghidra; copy-vs-compare semantics and direction convention UNKNOWN from the workspace text.
strcpy (returns length). Used in the save cluster for descriptor string/error-label handling, not for save payload fields.
strcmp-like byte compare (0=equal, 1=differ). Invoked by FUN_08015154 immediately after the transfer with arguments dropped by Ghidra; hypothesised to be the magic-string validity check.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot/reset: FUN_08000234 calls FUN_0801a6a8 before task registration. Loads the 0x2000-byte SRAM block at 0x0E000000 into the RAM mirror, then runs subsystem initialisers FUN_08019774, FUN_08019dd8 (stub), FUN_0801a3ac, FUN_08013e38, FUN_08014028(0), FUN_08015af0(0), FUN_0800310c(0).
ram_fields_updated: work struct head zeroed (*puVar1=0, bytes +4/+5, halfword +6)
~24 scattered bytes at literal-derived offsets zeroed
caller_chains.how_mapped: Seed FUN_0801a6a8 taken from ghidra/save_related_functions.c; edges cross-checked between ghidra/callgraph.json and the func_-spelled call sites in ghidra/decompiled.c (the JSON systematically misses func_-spelled edges, e.g. 0x08000234->0x0801a6a8 and 0x08015154->0x0801520c); every reached body read in full. Identity of the zeroed work struct (_DAT_0801a7e4) with the save mirror (_DAT_0801a818) is UNPROVEN (literal values absent from workspace) and is recorded as hypothesis, not fact.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Write/flush path (gameplay save trigger UNKNOWN): byte-copies the RAM mirror to SRAM at 0x0E000000 and verifies. No static caller exists in ghidra/callgraph.json; the ROM ends most functions with UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE dispatch, so the triggering caller cannot be closed from the given files.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Found by reading the descriptor-sharing siblings FUN_080151d0/FUN_0801520c in ghidra/decompiled.c and proving FUN_0801cc1c's direction from its body (param1 read, param2 written). Absence of callers confirmed by exhaustive query of ghidra/callgraph.json (147 nodes) and grep of ghidra/decompiled.c.

fields.name: magic_POKEMON_TAKASHI2

observed_values.cap-00-future-0.sav: ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff (blank)

fields.update_mechanism: Written only as part of the whole-block (0x2000-byte) verbatim flush of the RAM struct; presumed present in RAM from struct initialisation. Hypothesised load-time validity gate via strcmp-like FUN_08019f1c called from FUN_08015154 (arguments unrecovered).
fields.evidence: Bytes present verbatim in saves/cap-01-future-1.sav offset 0 and absent (0xFF) in blank saves/cap-00-future-0.sav (Python scan); sole SRAM transfer covers offset 0. Code-side gate is HYPOTHESIS: string literal does not appear in decompiled text; only the strcmp/strcpy machinery in FUN_08015154 supports the role.

fields.name: header_padding_zero
fields.update_mechanism: Whole-block flush; plausibly NUL terminator plus reserved tail of the magic string field in the RAM struct.
fields.evidence: All zero in the only populated sample (Python nonzero-byte scan: no non-zero bytes between 0x10 and 0x1F).

fields.name: header_word_0x20
fields.update_mechanism: Whole-block flush of the RAM struct. Field-level gameplay writer unknown: no function in the corpus can be tied to this offset because the RAM mirror base (_DAT_0801a818) is unresolved.
fields.evidence: struct.unpack('<I') at 0x20 in cap-01 gives 1. Semantics UNKNOWN: candidates are format version (=1) or a save-present/initialised flag; a generation counter is not supported (single sample, single copy, no selection logic in code).

fields.name: header_word_0x24
fields.update_mechanism: Whole-block flush of the RAM struct. Field-level gameplay writer unknown (unresolved RAM mirror base).
fields.evidence: struct.unpack('<I') at 0x24 in cap-01 gives 1. Semantics UNKNOWN: second version/flag word, slot state, or boolean stored as u32.

fields.name: header_word_0x28_rom_pointer_like
fields.update_mechanism: Whole-block flush; most plausibly a RAM struct field holding a ROM address at flush time, incidentally persisted by the verbatim copy. Field-level writer unknown.
fields.evidence: Value 0x084A1097 lies in the GBA ROM window (0x08000000.., ROM offset 0x4A1097). Rejected as a checksum: sum8=0xAA, sum16=0x05AA, sum32=0x05AA, xor8=0xB8, crc32=0x47F0D428, crc32-excluding-word=0x411A96A0, sum-u16le=0x5954, sum-u32le=0x207838DD over the cap-01 block - none equals 0x084A1097 (Python, both files, multiple ranges).

fields.name: payload_body_zero_in_sample

observed_values.cap-01-future-1.sav: 0x00 (all 8148 bytes zero; 8170 zero bytes total in the block)

fields.update_mechanism: Whole-block flush of the RAM struct. Internal sub-fields (presumed lesson/progress/settings members) cannot be delineated: every byte is at its zero value in the only populated sample.
fields.evidence: Python scan: only 22 non-zero bytes exist in the populated 0x2000 block (magic + offsets 0x20, 0x24, 0x28..0x2B). Claiming finer fields here would be fabrication.

fields.name: unused_sram_tail
fields.update_mechanism: Never transferred: outside the sole 0x2000-byte transfer at the only 0x0E000000 call site. Physically could hold three more 8 KiB blocks, but no code references them.
fields.evidence: Python: bytes 0x2000..0x7FFF are all 0xFF in both files; grep of ghidra/decompiled.c finds exactly one SRAM address literal (0xe000000 at FUN_0801a6a8's call).

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the magic is the load gate (FUN_08019f1c in FUN_08015154): save treated as absent, boot as blank. Unchanged behaviour falsifies the gate hypothesis. No checksum repair exists to apply.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Fill magic with 0xFF, leave body intact
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Erased-header save: same prediction as single-byte magic corruption; still loading would move the validity gate to header word 0x20/0x24.
Version word: 2/0xFFFFFFFF rejected or migrated. Present-flag: 0 boots as no-save, 2 loads. Distinguishes semantics of header_word_0x20.
Distinguishes flag vs counter vs second version word for header_word_0x24; no visible change in the near-empty save is the prediction for a pure flag.

If a dereferenced ROM pointer: null/wrong target crashes, hangs, or corrupts first use; ROM-start pointer changes data read. No change under all three demotes it to an opaque persisted word (still not a checksum unless rejection is also seen).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Fill zero body with 0xFF; separately fill with repeating 0x01
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Range-checked fields: unlock/corrupt lesson state or sanitised on load (post-session re-dump shows clamping). Identical boot + verbatim re-dump of the mutated body proves blind trust in the block.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write ASCII SECOND_SLOT_TEST at block midpoint
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Survives load untouched under the single-struct model; wiped by any save flush (whole-block rewrite). A half-only overwrite would reveal sub-block structure.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Copy the whole populated block (magic included) to offset 0x2000
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Ignored under the single-slot conclusion. If used after slot-0 magic corruption, a fallback slot exists and the geometry conclusion must be revised.

open_questions: RAM mirror base address: referenced only as _DAT_0801a818, whose literal value is absent from ghidra/decompiled.c. Closable in one step by searching EWRAM/IWRAM for 'POKEMON_TAKASHI2' after a boot load, or by resolving the literal pool at 0x0801a818 in the ROM.

Direction/semantics of the RAM-copied payload FUN_0801cda4 (UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE): is FUN_0801520c read or write, and is FUN_0801ccbc's second pass a byte-compare verify, and what does its third argument 0x94 mean?

Write trigger: FUN_080151d0 has no static caller in ghidra/callgraph.json. Which gameplay event (lesson completion, menu, autosave) flushes the save, and who sets the descriptor for that path? Closable with an SRAM write breakpoint at 0x0E000000 during play.

Semantics of header words at 0x20 (=1), 0x24 (=1) and 0x28 (=0x084A1097): version/flag/pointer readings are hypotheses; needs a non-empty save produced by real play (report fuzzing target F9) to resolve.
Internal layout of the 8148-byte zero body (offset 0x2C..0x1FFF): undelineable from a sample in which every byte is zero.
Is the work struct zeroed by FUN_0801a6a8 (_DAT_0801a7e4) the same RAM struct as the save mirror (_DAT_0801a818)? If yes, exactly which of its zeroed offsets correspond to save fields?

Packet profile summary mentions 6 .sav files but only 2 (one blank, one near-empty) are present in saves/; findings rest on those 2 and should be re-checked against richer populated saves if they become available.
No paired emulator save states (.ss) exist in states/ for this title, so all fuzzing predictions are specified for cold-boot reload of mutated .sav images rather than save-state reload.
